insight.title: Fungi Prioritize Resources Through Pulsing Signals
insight.subtitle: Beneath the forest floor, fungal networks manage their vast infrastructure using rhythmic electrical pulses to route nutrients where they are needed most.
insight.notificationHook: Fungi signal like a power grid

sections.text: Hidden beneath the soil, massive fungal colonies operate like a living, breathing power grid. They use rhythmic, internal electrical signals to sense which parts of the forest require sugar, water, or chemical defense.

When a specific area becomes depleted, the fungal network adjusts its flow, shifting resources toward the deficit. It acts as an organic load-balancer, constantly recalibrating the forest’s metabolism to ensure total survival.

This system requires no central command. By responding to local feedback loops, the network creates an incredibly efficient, self-healing supply chain that covers miles of terrain without wasting a single calorie.
The forest stays balanced through constant, rhythmic negotiation.
